COPERNICUS_SHIFTED_CENTER.title: A Different Center
COPERNICUS_SHIFTED_CENTER.pages.INVITATI: A later reader brings two fictional travel tables, drawing on Copernicus's solar reference to discuss apparent retrograde motion. They point to existing exits on your current map: A: {ExitA}; B: {ExitB}. This practice uses no new Fixed or Question slot. Actually following a table gives up the other path's normal opportunity.
Choose a reference, then decide whether to follow it. Use no new Fixed or Question slot.
Close the invitation and choose your path normally on the map.
COPERNICUS_SHIFTED_CENTER.pages.REFERENC: The old table treats the ground as stationary and points to A: {ExitA}. The solar table includes Earth's and the observer's motion and points to B: {ExitB}. Keeping the old table is a valid choice. These fictional travel tables promise neither supplies nor shortcuts.
Examine its residual errors without reordering the three entries. You may still withdraw afterward.
Include Earth's and the observer's motion and reorder the three entries. You may still withdraw afterward.
COPERNICUS_SHIFTED_CENTER.pages.ORDER_FI: The solar reference includes the observer's displacement in the explanation. Place three entries in order: observer displacement, planetary motion, and apparent retrograde motion. Which comes first? Current order: {Order}.
Record the motion of Earth and the observer upon it.
Record the planet's own motion, to compare with observer displacement and apparent retrograde motion.
COPERNICUS_SHIFTED_CENTER.pages.ORDER_AF: Observer displacement is recorded. Place planetary motion next, or first record the apparent backward motion. Current order: {Order}.
Record the planet's own motion, to compare with observer displacement and apparent retrograde motion.
Record the apparent backward motion, to compare with the motions of the observer and planet.
Planetary motion is recorded. Place observer displacement next, or first record the apparent backward motion. Current order: {Order}.
Record the motion of Earth and the observer upon it.
Record the apparent backward motion, to compare with the motions of the observer and planet.
COPERNICUS_SHIFTED_CENTER.pages.LAST_OBS: Add observer displacement as the final entry, keeping the three entries distinct. Current order: {Order}.
Record the motion of Earth and the observer upon it.
COPERNICUS_SHIFTED_CENTER.pages.LAST_PLA: Add planetary motion as the final entry, keeping the three entries distinct. Current order: {Order}.
Record the planet's own motion, to compare with observer displacement and apparent retrograde motion.
COPERNICUS_SHIFTED_CENTER.pages.LAST_APP: Add apparent retrograde motion as the final entry, recording the phenomenon to be explained. Current order: {Order}.
Record the apparent backward motion, to compare with the motions of the observer and planet.
COPERNICUS_SHIFTED_CENTER.pages.RESIDUAL: The old table explains apparent retrograde motion with stationary ground. Residual errors in periods and stellar positions remain. Record those errors and note that this account cannot predict supplies on the mountain paths.
Keep the period and stellar-position errors, noting that they cannot predict path supplies; then decide whether to leave.
Return to normal map choice. Neither A nor B is forced.

COPERNICUS_SHIFTED_CENTER.pages.ROUTE_OR: The residual errors are recorded. The old table points to current exit A: {ExitA}; the other exit is B: {ExitB}. Following the table immediately takes A and gives up B's normal opportunity this time, with no promise of extra supplies.
Follow the old table: take A.
Immediately enter current exit A, giving up B's normal opportunity this time. No extra reward is promised.
Return to normal map choice. Neither A nor B is forced.
COPERNICUS_SHIFTED_CENTER.pages.ROUTE_SO: Order: {Order}; the residual errors are recorded. The solar table points to current exit B: {ExitB}; the other exit is A: {ExitA}. Following it immediately takes B and gives up A's normal opportunity this time, with no promise of extra supplies.
Follow the solar table: take B.
Immediately enter current exit B, giving up A's normal opportunity this time. No extra reward is promised.
Return to normal map choice. Neither A nor B is forced.
COPERNICUS_SHIFTED_CENTER.pages.RESULT_D: You decline the comparison. No path is chosen automatically and no new Fixed or Question slot is used. Return to the map and choose your route normally.
Close the practice and choose a current map exit normally.
COPERNICUS_SHIFTED_CENTER.pages.RESULT_W: You end the practice, keeping your choices and any records already made. Neither exit is forced. Return to the map and choose your route normally.
Close the practice and choose a current map exit normally.
COPERNICUS_SHIFTED_CENTER.pages.TRAVEL_R: Your table and residual-error record are saved. You are leaving by the existing exit you confirmed, giving up the other path's normal opportunity this time.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.title: A Ledger of Four Errors
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.INVITATION.des: The miners' ledger holds two initial samples: rich ore from a warm site and poor ore from a cold site. The old prediction therefore promises rich ore wherever it is warm. A later commentary on Bacon asks how that inference arose. This uses the third act's Fixed opportunity; declining closes it too.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.INVITATION.opt: Use the third Fixed opportunity. Choose a check, then collect a real counterexample sample before deciding whether to replace the old discount.
Spend the third Fixed opportunity and retain the original route's ending and the Tablet's old discount.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.BIAS.descripti: The two initial samples confound temperature with ore quality. They do not warrant the general prediction. Which misleading habit will you examine first? Choosing a check gives no immunity to other biases.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.BIAS.options.C: Check the Idols of the Tribe.
People project general order from a few tidy cases. Test the leap from warm samples to guaranteed rich ore.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.COUNTEREXAMPLE: You check the human tendency to project general order from a few tidy cases. The initial samples are warm and rich, cold and poor. You must still collect warm, poor ore to test the claim that warmth guarantees rich ore; a proposed test is not a collected sample.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.DECISION_TRIBE: You have collected warm, poor ore. It breaks the tidy rule that warmth guarantees rich ore, without proving that temperature has no bearing at all. This check corrects one overgeneralization. Decide how far the report may reach.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_LIMITED: The warm, poor counterexample breaks the tidy prediction. Your report covers only the sampled area. Replace the old discount: on each combat's first turn, if your first two manual cards are different types among Attack, Skill, and Power, draw 2 after the second resolves.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_CONTROL: You collect an ambient-temperature, poor-ore control beside warm, poor ore, deferring a general temperature rule. Replace the old discount and wait until each combat's second turn: if your first two manual cards are different types among Attack, Skill, and Power, draw 3 after the second resolves.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_KEPT_TR: You keep the prediction, publishing its two initial samples and the warm, poor counterexample. Their conflict remains. Adopt no new method. Retain the original route's ending and old discount; the third Fixed opportunity is spent.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.BIAS.options.C: Check the Idols of the Cave.
A familiar miner and familiar sites may narrow your judgment. Check the reach of personal experience.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.COUNTEREXAMPLE: You check how personal experience confines judgment. The familiar miner's warm-rich and cold-poor samples may cover only the sites they know. You must still collect warm, poor ore. Trust in a person does not make their experience cover every site.
You have collected warm, poor ore beyond the familiar miner's two initial samples. This does not make the miner untrustworthy in every matter; it shows that familiar experience cannot guarantee rich ore wherever it is warm. Decide the report's scope.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_LIMITED: Your report adds warm, poor ore beyond the familiar miner's experience, covering only the sampled area. Replace the old discount: on each combat's first turn, if your first two manual cards are different types among Attack, Skill, and Power, draw 2 after the second resolves.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_CONTROL: You collect an ambient-temperature, poor-ore control beyond the familiar miner's experience, deferring generalization. Replace the old discount and wait until each combat's second turn: if your first two manual cards are different types among Attack, Skill, and Power, draw 3 after the second resolves.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_KEPT_CA: You keep the familiar miner's prediction, publishing its limited experience and the warm, poor counterexample. Adopt no new method. Retain the original route's ending and old discount; the third Fixed opportunity is spent.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.BIAS.options.C: Check the Idols of the Market.
Different speakers may lack a shared measure for 'rich ore.' Check how words can mislead the inference.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.COUNTEREXAMPLE: You check confusion introduced by language. The miner and clerk may use 'rich ore' without a shared measure; a common name cannot replace a common check. You must still collect warm, poor ore and retain its specific conditions beside the initial samples.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.DECISION_MARKE: You have collected warm, poor ore. The ledger records each sample's conditions instead of letting 'rich ore' guarantee every site. The counterexample defeats that guarantee, but renaming alone establishes no complete measure. Decide the report's scope.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_LIMITED: Your report covers the three samples' area; a shared measure for 'rich ore' remains to be checked. Replace the old discount: on each combat's first turn, if your first two manual cards are different types among Attack, Skill, and Power, draw 2 after the second resolves.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_CONTROL: An ambient-temperature, poor-ore control is recorded. A shared measure for 'rich ore' still needs checking; generalization waits. Replace the old discount and wait until each combat's second turn: if your first two manual cards are different types among Attack, Skill, and Power, draw 3 after the second resolves.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_KEPT_MA: You keep the prediction, publishing its unverified shared measure for 'rich ore' and the warm, poor counterexample. Adopt no new method. Retain the original route's ending and old discount; the third Fixed opportunity is spent.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.BIAS.options.C: Check the Idols of the Theatre.
A received system may assign the conclusion before examining samples. Check how it arranges the facts.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.COUNTEREXAMPLE: You check how a received system arranges facts. The old account treats warm-rich and cold-poor samples as necessary confirmation, leaving no place for an exception. You must still collect warm, poor ore; merely opposing authority is no completed test.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.DECISION_THEAT: You have collected warm, poor ore. The old system cannot retain only its two convenient initial samples and exclude the new record. The counterexample breaks its guarantee without instantly establishing another complete system. Decide the report's scope.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_LIMITED: The counterexample breaks the old system's guarantee. Your report covers only the sampled area. Replace the old discount: on each combat's first turn, if your first two manual cards are different types among Attack, Skill, and Power, draw 2 after the second resolves.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_CONTROL: You collect an ambient-temperature, poor-ore control. The old system's guarantee needs rechecking; generalization waits. Replace the old discount and wait until each combat's second turn: if your first two manual cards are different types among Attack, Skill, and Power, draw 3 after the second resolves.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_KEPT_TH: You keep the prediction, publishing its system's assumptions and the conflicting warm, poor counterexample. Adopt no new method. Retain the original route's ending and old discount; the third Fixed opportunity is spent.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.COUNTEREXAMPLE: Retrieve the warm, poor counterexample sample.
Actually collect warm, poor ore and add it to the ledger. This step adopts no new method yet.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.DECISION.optio: Report only the sampled area; replace the Tablet's old cost discount. If the first two manual cards on each combat's first turn are different types among Attack, Skill, and Power, draw 2.
Take an ambient-temperature, poor-ore control sample.
Actually add a control and defer generalization; replace the old discount. If the first two manual cards on each combat's second turn are different types among Attack, Skill, and Power, draw 3.
Keep the old prediction, publishing its premise and counterexample.
Adopt no new method; retain the original route's ending and the Tablet's old cost discount. The third Fixed opportunity is still spent.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_DECLINE: You decline, collecting no new samples. The third Fixed opportunity is spent; retain the original route's ending and the Tablet's old discount.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_LIMITED: Keep the collected samples, chosen check, and limits of the report on record.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_CONTROL: Keep the collected samples, chosen check, and limits of the report on record.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_KEPT.op: Keep the collected samples, chosen check, and limits of the report on record.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_DECLINE: Keep the refusal and the Tablet's old discount on record.
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.title: Luther: A Signature and a Neighbor
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.pages.INVITATION.desc: Beside the waystation's register, a later reader brings Luther's writing on freedom and service to a neighbor. The clerk asks you to endorse the station's public arrangements. You may read first, check the commitment's scope, sign immediately, or stay out.
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.pages.INVITATION.opti: Use this act's Question. A route switch still requires a later act of help.
Keep this act's Question and Augustine's route. This invitation will not return.
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.pages.DECLARATION.des: The register asks you to support all of the station's public arrangements. You may read the text, ask what the commitment covers, or sign at once. Your initial action will remain on record even if you later change your position.
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.pages.DECLARATION.opt: Record that you have read, without signing yet; then examine the arrangements' effects.
Record your inquiry, without signing yet. Checking alone provides no care.
Sign for all the terms first.
Record a full signature. Changing your position later will not erase it.
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.pages.NEED_READ.descr: You read the text without signing. Now its effect is clear: a companion who has not signed every term is excluded from this round of care. They need water and bedding. You may change your commitment and help in person, or accept the arrangement. Refusing to sign alone provides no care.
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.pages.NEED_CHECKED.de: You checked the commitment's scope without signing. The clerk confirms that a companion who has not signed every term receives no care this time. They need water and bedding. Your inquiry has not met that need. You must still accept the arrangement or change your commitment and help in person.
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.pages.NEED_SIGNED.des: You signed for every term. Now its effect is clear: a companion who has not signed every term is excluded from care and needs water and bedding. You may append a refusal, narrow your commitment, or keep your signature. The original signature remains. Changing your words alone provides no help.
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.pages.NEED.options.RE: Refuse the whole commitment and prepare to help.
Carrying water or bedding must follow before switching. Then lose Augustine's first-turn benefit; keep the Seal's base practice.
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.pages.NEED.options.LI: Narrow the commitment and prepare to help.
Commit only to care you can undertake. Actual help switches the route and gives up Augustine's first-turn benefit.
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.pages.NEED.options.KE: Accept the terms and sign publicly.
Keep an existing signature or sign now. Provide no care; keep Augustine and his benefit. The Question remains spent.
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.pages.SERVICE_REFUSED: You refuse the whole commitment. If you signed earlier, that signature remains beside the appended refusal. Freedom has not poured water for your companion. You must still carry water or bedding to switch to Self and Other. Help does not purchase salvation.
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.pages.SERVICE_LIMITED: You limit the commitment to care you can undertake; your initial action remains in the register. Narrowing a promise does not remove the responsibility before you. You must still carry water or bedding to switch to Self and Other. Help does not purchase salvation.
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.pages.SERVICE.options: Help and switch to Luther. Lose Augustine's 6 Block or 1 Energy on each first turn and the choices following his route; keep the Seal's base practice.
Help and switch to Luther. Lose Augustine's 6 Block or 1 Energy on each first turn and the choices following his route; keep the Seal's base practice.
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.pages.RESULT_SWITCHED: You bring water to your companion. This act is recorded beside your unchanged initial action. The route switches to Luther's Self and Other: give up Augustine's 6 Block or 1 Energy on each combat's first turn and the choices following his former route. The Civic Seal's base practice remains. Help purchases no salvation and grants no extra combat reward.

You carry bedding to your companion. This act is recorded beside your unchanged initial action. The route switches to Luther's Self and Other: give up Augustine's 6 Block or 1 Energy on each combat's first turn and the choices following his former route. The Civic Seal's base practice remains. Help purchases no salvation and grants no extra combat reward.
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.pages.RESULT_KEPT.des: You accept the public terms and keep or add your signature. You bring your companion neither water nor bedding; they still lack this round of care. Augustine's route and first-turn benefit remain. This act's Question is spent. A signature alone is no act of help.
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.pages.RESULT_DECLINED: You stay out of the registration. Augustine's route, its benefit, and this act's Question remain available. No route switch occurs, and no act of care is attributed to you.
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.pages.RESULT_SWITCHED: Keep the initial action, final response, and actual care on record.
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.pages.RESULT_KEPT.opt: Keep the signature and the absence of care on record. The Question is not refunded.
LUTHER_SIGNED_CARE.pages.RESULT_DECLINED: Close this invitation and keep this act's Question.
MACHIAVELLI_FLOOD_PREPARATION.title: Machiavelli: Before the Wind Changes
MACHIAVELLI_FLOOD_PREPARATION.pages.INVI: Carrying the Uncarved Stone, you read an archive comparing Rousseau with the earlier Machiavelli, not a meeting or line of influence. A town has kept the same riverside deployment for years. The weather is fair; its limited labour can prepare one measure. This is your second-act fixed opportunity.
MACHIAVELLI_FLOOD_PREPARATION.pages.PREP: The flood has not happened. You can reinforce the bank or coordinate an evacuation, but not both. Your choice commits the labour now. It cannot be changed after the result is revealed.
MACHIAVELLI_FLOOD_PREPARATION.pages.FLOO: The river suddenly changes course. The reinforced reach reduces the impact, but without evacuation coordination the crews scatter and another reach is damaged. Preparation mattered without controlling all of fortune. A bold decision now cannot count as a bank built earlier.

The river suddenly changes course. Coordinators evacuate residents, but cannot protect the unreinforced works. You retain some capacity to act while losing facilities. Preparation mattered without controlling all of fortune.
MACHIAVELLI_FLOOD_PREPARATION.pages.RESU: You adopt Machiavelli’s historical practice, keeping the limits of the bank preparation visible. The stone no longer grants convention discounts or their enemy Strength cost. Each combat, if your first manual card on turn 1 is a Skill, gain 8 Block at the start of turn 2. A different first card forfeits this combat’s benefit.

You adopt Machiavelli’s historical practice, keeping the limits of coordination visible. The stone no longer grants convention discounts or their enemy Strength cost. Each combat, if your first manual card on turn 1 is an Attack, gain 2 Energy at the start of turn 2. A different first card forfeits this combat’s benefit.

You retain Rousseau. The archive still records the reduced impact at the bank and inadequate evacuation; it cannot become a complete success. The stone keeps its original convention practice. This act’s fixed opportunity is spent.

You retain Rousseau. The archive still records the evacuation and the damaged works; it cannot become a complete success. The stone keeps its original convention practice. This act’s fixed opportunity is spent.
You decline this fixed opportunity, retaining Rousseau and the stone’s convention practice. The second-act fixed opportunity is spent. No institutional 017 question has been completed.
MACHIAVELLI_FLOOD_PREPARATION.pages.INVI: Enter this act’s fixed proposal; decide whether to adopt it after the result.
Decline the second-act fixed opportunity; keep the original convention practice.
MACHIAVELLI_FLOOD_PREPARATION.pages.PREP: Forgo evacuation coordination. If adopted: a first manual Skill prepares 8 Block for turn 2.
Forgo bank reinforcement. If adopted: a first manual Attack prepares 2 Energy for turn 2.
MACHIAVELLI_FLOOD_PREPARATION.pages.FLOO: Adopt Machiavelli; replace convention effects with the selected delayed preparation.
Keep convention discounts and their enemy Strength cost; this fixed opportunity is still spent.
MACHIAVELLI_FLOOD_PREPARATION.pages.RESU: Keep the preparation and its limited consequences.
Keep the preparation and its limited consequences.
Keep the preparation and its limited consequences.
OCKHAM_NAMES_INQUIRY.title: Ockham: The Extra Names
OCKHAM_NAMES_INQUIRY.pages.INVITATION.de: A station clerk has counted every occurrence of “bridge worker” as another supply claimant. A later commentary by Ockham asks what the term stands for in each sentence. You still carry the Category Tablet.
OCKHAM_NAMES_INQUIRY.pages.INVITATION.op: Decline this act’s fixed opportunity and spend its question. Your current doctrine stays.
Keep both second-act opportunities. This invitation will not return.
OCKHAM_NAMES_INQUIRY.pages.AUDIT.descrip: There is time to inspect one entry. The same expression appears in three sentences, with explicitly different uses. Which entry will you check?
OCKHAM_NAMES_INQUIRY.pages.AUDIT.options: Check the people designated in this distribution entry.
Here the clerk means the mental classification, not another worker.
“Bridge worker is written on the board.”
Here the expression is quoted as writing, not used to claim timber.
OCKHAM_NAMES_INQUIRY.pages.DISCREPANCY_W: You check worker A’s signed receipt; worker B has not signed. The clerk also counted the classification and the quoted inscription as people. Only your chosen entry has been inspected in detail; the other entries remain unchecked. A word’s use in this sentence matters: words and concepts can themselves be designated by other terms.
OCKHAM_NAMES_INQUIRY.pages.DISCREPANCY.o: Keep the tablet’s cost-category rule; leave the other entries for review.
Replace broad cost categories with the narrow named-card rule: next 2 manual same-model cards cost 2 less. Other names get no discount.
Keep cost-category discounts without treating unchecked entries as proved.
OCKHAM_NAMES_INQUIRY.pages.DISCREPANCY_C: This entry explicitly discusses the classification in thought. It adds no worker to the timber queue. A’s signed receipt and B’s missing signature remain on the ledger; you have not checked them in detail. Nor have you inspected the inscription entry. A concept is not automatically “simple supposition”: the term’s use in the sentence matters.
OCKHAM_NAMES_INQUIRY.pages.DISCREPANCY_I: Here “bridge worker” is quoted as an inscription. It is not another timber claimant. A’s signed receipt and B’s missing signature remain on the ledger; you have not checked them in detail. Nor have you inspected the classification entry. Referring to writing does not always mean material supposition: a term can also signify written things.
OCKHAM_NAMES_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_DECLIN: You leave the ledger unopened. Your tablet and both second-act opportunities remain.
Keep the recorded limits and decision.
OCKHAM_NAMES_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_ANNOTA: You annotate the one entry you inspected; the others remain marked for review. The tablet keeps its broad cost-category rule. The question is spent. A local correction does not certify the whole ledger.
Keep the recorded limits and decision.
You limit distribution to the verified list, leaving broader claims unresolved. The tablet now uses a narrow named-card rule instead of cost categories: each turn, its first manual non-X Attack, Skill or Power names a card; the next 2 manually played non-X cards of that model cost 2 less, to a minimum of 0. A zero-cost first card gives no discount this turn. Matching a card model is a game rule, not a claim that names and individuals are identical.
Keep the recorded limits and decision.
OCKHAM_NAMES_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_KEPT.d: You preserve the old cost-category rule and mark the unverified entries as unverified. No new supply reward is certified. The question is spent; keeping a practice does not establish its truth.
OCKHAM_NAMES_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_KEPT.o: Keep the recorded limits and decision.
GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.title: Gorgias: The Sealed Crate
A sealed crate bears the label “grain”. No one has inspected its contents. Gorgias asks what speech can make a crowd do, and what it cannot establish. This uses your remaining question.
Spend this act’s question on one public claim.
Spend the question without testing this claim.
GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.pages.SPEECH.desc: People await a grain delivery. You know only the label and unbroken seal. What will you tell them?
GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.pages.SPEECH.opti: “The grain is here. Distribute it now.”
Gain quick agreement while claiming an unverified fact.
“The label says grain. Open it first.”
Keep the evidence boundary; distribution waits.
Spend the question without making a claim.
GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.pages.STRONG_CLAI: The crowd agrees to distribute the crate at once. Your words changed their plan, but no one opened it. What does their agreement show?
Infer the contents from the crowd’s assent.
The speech moved them; the contents remain unknown.
GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.pages.CAUTIOUS_CL: The crowd delays distribution and asks to open the crate. Your careful words changed their plan, but no one has opened it yet. What does the delay show?
Treat delay as proof of absence.
Infer an empty crate from the crowd’s caution.
The speech slowed them; the contents remain unknown.
You used the crowd’s reaction as evidence about the crate. Agreement does not put grain inside; delay does not remove it. The label and seal still need inspection.
Keep this question without changing your route.
Leave this speech without a new route claim.
GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.pages.BELIEF_ONLY: You distinguish a change in belief from knowledge of the contents. Speech can move action before inspection; whether grain is inside remains open.
Keep this question without changing your route.
Leave this speech without a new route claim.
GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_RECO: You record a limited question about persuasion and knowledge. Aristotle remains your current route; the tablet and combat practice remain.
GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_KEPT: You keep the category practice without a new account. This act’s question is spent; your route and relic remain.
GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_STOP: You stop before making a claim. The question is spent; your current route remains.
GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_DECL: You decline the inquiry. The question is spent; your current route remains.
ANAXAGORAS_MIXTURE_INQUIRY.title: Anaxagoras: Order in the Mixture
ANAXAGORAS_MIXTURE_INQUIRY.pages.INVITAT: You kept Parmenides rather than adopting the atomist account. Anaxagoras asks whether an already mixed world can change without anything coming from nothing. This uses your remaining question.
Spend this question to test a parallel explanation.
Spend this question and keep Parmenides.
ANAXAGORAS_MIXTURE_INQUIRY.pages.MIXTURE: Imagine a mixture in which one visible color dominates. Will you explain the appearance by its greater share, or demand a completely pure portion? The visible example cannot prove that every ingredient is everywhere.
Keep unseen shares possible without claiming to have observed them.
Test what a claim of universal mixture would forbid.
Leave the account untested and spend this question.
ANAXAGORAS_MIXTURE_INQUIRY.pages.PREDOMI: A greater share can explain why this color appears, but cannot prove that every possible ingredient was present. What explanatory role will you demand of Mind?
Leave local arrangements to further material explanation.
Require an account of every result.
Ask why each arrangement is the best one.
ANAXAGORAS_MIXTURE_INQUIRY.pages.PURE_DE: If every portion still contains every ingredient, a completely pure piece cannot be drawn from this model. That is a theoretical burden, not a result established by these colors. What will Mind explain?
Leave local arrangements to further material explanation.
Require an account of every result.
Ask why each arrangement is the best one.
ANAXAGORAS_MIXTURE_INQUIRY.pages.MIND_ST: You limit Mind to starting the motion that separates the mixture. Later local arrangements still need an account; the start alone does not explain why each one is best.
Keep the mixture and Mind as an open comparison, not a new route.
Do not record a new explanatory account.
ANAXAGORAS_MIXTURE_INQUIRY.pages.MIND_EV: You demand that Mind explain why each particular arrangement is best. Plato later criticizes this promise as unfulfilled; do not put that criticism in Anaxagoras’s own mouth.
Keep the mixture and Mind as an open comparison, not a new route.
Do not record a new explanatory account.
ANAXAGORAS_MIXTURE_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_: You record a limited question about mixture and Mind. Parmenides remains your current route. No graph turn, relic, or combat reward follows.
You keep Parmenides without recording a new account. This act’s question is spent; the current route and relic remain.
You stop before settling the explanation. The question is spent; Parmenides remains.

EMPEDOCLES_ROOTS_INQUIRY.title: Empedocles: Four Roots in Relation

Establish order with a Skill or Power before attacking.

MACHIAVELLI_REALIST_CHALLENGE.title: Machiavelli: The Realist's Question

HOBBES_AUTHORIZED_SOVEREIGNTY.title: Hobbes: After Authorization

LOCKE_CARGO_IDENTITY.title: Locke: Who Took the Cargo Box?

LOCKE_CARGO_IDENTITY.pages.EVIDENCE_SIGN: The signature chain is continuous, but the witness's memory and the physical mark remain unchecked. The new evidence separates person from office: a valid signature proves the office, not the person.
LOCKE_CARGO_IDENTITY.pages.EVIDENCE_MARK: The physical mark matches, but the witness's memory and the signature chain remain unchecked. The new evidence separates person from office: the box is the same, not necessarily the keeper.
LOCKE_CARGO_IDENTITY.pages.RESULT_MEMORY: You return the box on the witness's verifiable memory and give up the other checks. LOCKE_CARGO_IDENTITY.pages.INVITATION.op: [Memory] Verify the witness's memory; give up the signature and mark checks.

HUME_INDUCTION.title: Hume: Will Tomorrow Be the Same?

HUME_INDUCTION.pages.TEST_HABIT.descript: You buy a pass on habit. The fourth bell brings a repair crew instead of an opening. Custom predicted the gate, not the repair.
HUME_INDUCTION.pages.RESULT_REPAIR.descr: You repair first and spend 75 gold. You enter Hume's node: each combat, after four manual cards in two alternating pairs, draw 2. The record keeps the observed sequence without asserting necessity.

WOLLSTONECRAFT_ADMISSION.title: Wollstonecraft: One Threshold, Two Applications
WOLLSTONECRAFT_ADMISSION.pages.INVITATIO: Two apprentices with comparable work apply for the same course. An old admission clause quietly demands more proof from one of them. Compare their completed work first; then decide whether to unify the published conditions, fund a fair evaluation for both, or keep the old practice and record an exclusion you cannot explain. WOLLSTONECRAFT_ADMISSION.pages.RESULT_UN: You publish one admission condition for both and give up your recommendation priority. WOLLSTONECRAFT_ADMISSION.pages.RESULT_FU: You spend your own evaluation slot so both applicants receive the same assessment. You enter Wollstonecraft's node with the practice; the record shows the cost borne by you, not by the excluded applicant.

KANT_APPERCEPTION.title: Kant: Can One 'I Think' Accompany Every Representation?
KANT_APPERCEPTION.pages.INVITATION.descr: A memory archive is stitched from scattered testimonies. Each clerk claims a different person; to call the archive one person, every testimony must be able to carry the same 'I think'. But a public rule of unity may erase the witnesses' differences. This is the act-three fixed opportunity.
KANT_APPERCEPTION.pages.EVIDENCE.descrip: The testimonies can be unified under one formal 'I think', but the unity is a condition of knowledge, not a proof that the persons are the same. You can make the rule constitutive of the archive, or keep it regulative and record the difference.
KANT_APPERCEPTION.pages.RESULT_CONSTITUT: You make the 'I think' a constitutive rule: every testimony must be logged under one public subject. You enter Kant's self node: each combat, after three manual cards with one Attack, one Skill and one Power, draw 2. The record claims formal unity, not a hidden substance.
KANT_APPERCEPTION.pages.RESULT_REGULATIV: You keep the unity regulative: the archive is read as if one subject accompanied it, while the scattered testimonies remain visible. You enter Kant's self node with the practice; the record separates formal unity from metaphysical claim.
KANT_APPERCEPTION.pages.RESULT_KEPT.desc: You keep Hume's bundle and decline the fixed opportunity. The act-three fixed slot is spent; the Kant self route is not completed.
KANT_APPERCEPTION.pages.INVITATION.optio: [Inspect] Read the scattered records before deciding.
[Decline] Keep Hume; spend the act-three fixed slot.
KANT_APPERCEPTION.pages.EVIDENCE.options: [Constitutive] One public 'I think' governs the archive.
[Regulative] Read the archive as if one subject accompanied it.
ROUSSEAU_CONSENT.title: Rousseau: Who Consented to the Custom?
ROUSSEAU_CONSENT.pages.INVITATION.descri: The entry relic has no recorded card-kind convention, so the proposal is explicit about insufficient data: the company wants to turn a practice into a public rule for everyone. First state whether your own practice accepts the same constraint; a new fact shows a companion cannot act that way. ROUSSEAU_CONSENT.pages.CONVENTION.descri: No card-kind record exists; the convention is marked as insufficient data. The companion's inability is a real counterexample, not a private preference. You can write a universal exception, keep the practice personal, or impose it and preserve the dispute.
You write a rule with an exception entry for everyone and give up one discount. You enter Rousseau's node: each combat, after three manual cards of distinct names but the same kind, draw 1 and gain 3 Block. The record states the excluded companion and the exception.
ROUSSEAU_CONSENT.pages.RESULT_PERSONAL.d: You keep the practice personal and do not make it law. You enter Rousseau's node with the practice; the record refuses to call a private custom a general will.

KANT_UNIVERSALIZATION.title: Kant: Is the Exception Yours Alone?
KANT_UNIVERSALIZATION.pages.INVITATION.d: You are offered one private fast lane, but the gate office wants to write 'only I may be the exception' into public rules. First state your maxim: it applies to everyone, only in emergencies, or only to yourself. Then you see other parties queue under the same maxim. KANT_UNIVERSALIZATION.pages.MAXIM.descri: The maxim is on the record. A universal rule costs your exemption; a public emergency exception costs a verification slot and must be reviewable; a private exception leaves the affected parties' loss visible. The system will not score your moral purity.

MILL_HARM.title: Mill: Does Offense Count as Harm?
MILL_HARM.pages.INVITATION.description: A guild wants to ban a minority experiment because it offends the majority. Apply the harm principle: does the experiment harm others, or only offend them? BEAUVOIR_OTHER.title: Beauvoir: Is She Only the Other?

FICHTE_SELF_POSITING.title: Fichte: Who Posits the Rule?
FICHTE_SELF_POSITING.pages.INVITATION.de: Kant's equal rule is written on the gate ledger, but the clerks who must follow it were never asked to author it. Fichte's objection is not that every impulse should become law: the self posits itself, but it also meets a check from what it is not. JAMES_FORCED_BRIDGE.title: The Bridge You Must Cross First

CAMUS_REVOLT_LIMIT.title: The Limit of Revolt

CARNAP_FRAMEWORK_CHOICE.title: Change the Format of the Question

AUSTIN_SPEECH_ACT.title: Does Saying It Make It So?
AUSTIN_SPEECH_ACT.pages.STATION.descript: At the shift-change station, the standard words are “I hand over the key.” The key is still in the locked cabinet. AUSTIN_SPEECH_ACT.pages.RESULT_PENDING.d: You record the utterance as an unfulfilled promise. It remains visible, but it does not open the cabinet or grant passage; later performance would need its own conditions.
POPPER_FALSIFICATION.title: The Dangerous Prediction
POPPER_FALSIFICATION.pages.REPORTS.descr: Two reports on a bridge's load limit sit on the table. One states a clear weight at which it would fail; the other says any outcome can be explained as success. Choose a test that could actually make the original report wrong.
POPPER_FALSIFICATION.pages.REPORTS.optio: Make a prediction that can fail before the bridge is used.
Accept the report that explains any outcome.
Keep a report that cannot fail; it cannot guide a risky crossing.
POPPER_FALSIFICATION.pages.EVIDENCE.desc: The load test is ready, but the tester itself may be damaged. A failed reading would not by itself settle whether the bridge or the instrument is at fault. Decide what this test can support.
POPPER_FALSIFICATION.pages.EVIDENCE.opti: Calibrate the instrument and report the failure risk.
Spend 12 gold to make the test usable; report a bounded failure risk, not certainty.
Publish the current counterexample with its unknown auxiliary conditions.
Show the failed prediction without pretending the whole theory is already dead.
Refuse to treat this test as the theory's end.
Keep the report provisional; record that one test does not settle a complex theory.
POPPER_FALSIFICATION.pages.RESULT_UNFALS: You chose the report that can explain any outcome. It offers no usable prediction; the crossing is delayed, and no “immunity” is gained. The record marks the report as unfalsifiable, not as meaningless.
POPPER_FALSIFICATION.pages.RESULT_CALIBR: You spend 12 gold to calibrate the instrument and report a bounded failure risk. The report is corrigible: it says what would count against it, without promising that the bridge can never hurt you.
POPPER_FALSIFICATION.pages.RESULT_COUNTE: You publish the current counterexample and mark the auxiliary conditions as unknown. The failed prediction counts against the report, but it does not by itself prove the whole theory false.
POPPER_FALSIFICATION.pages.RESULT_NOT_CO: You refuse to treat one test as the theory's end. The report stays provisional; the record keeps the test conditions and the unresolved auxiliary assumptions rather than declaring a final victory.
BERKELEY_PERCEIVED_MARK.title: Berkeley: The Mark No One Saw
BERKELEY_PERCEIVED_MARK.pages.INVITATION: A storeroom behind the shop; a screen hides a second consignment. You may check only one kind of evidence: touch it, knock and listen, or check the receipt.
Feel the surface and the weight behind the screen.
Knock on the crates and listen to what answers.
Compare the written consignment with what is behind the screen.
BERKELEY_PERCEIVED_MARK.pages.OBSERVED.d: Your one channel confirms the goods behind the screen, and in the same place you find a second object the keeper hid. The earlier explanation cannot cover it. You still need not declare that no objects exist.
BERKELEY_PERCEIVED_MARK.pages.OBSERVED.o: Refuse the claim that the hidden object must be a material substance, without concluding that nothing exists.
Spend one shop purchase opportunity (75 gold) to have a second observer check the same place.
Record only what was observed and refuse a verdict on the underlying entity.
BERKELEY_PERCEIVED_MARK.pages.RESULT_REJ: You reject "unseen" as proof of "non-existent" and record only that the present evidence is insufficient.
BERKELEY_PERCEIVED_MARK.pages.RESULT_WIT: A second observer confirms both objects; 75 gold is spent, the price of one shop purchase.
BERKELEY_PERCEIVED_MARK.pages.RESULT_SCO: You keep only the observable mark and refuse a verdict on the entity behind the screen.
BERKELEY_PERCEIVED_MARK.pages.RESULT_REJ: Close the record without a further verdict.
BERKELEY_PERCEIVED_MARK.pages.RESULT_WIT: Close the record without a further verdict.
BERKELEY_PERCEIVED_MARK.pages.RESULT_SCO: Close the record without a further verdict.
MONTESQUIEU_BALANCE.title: Montesquieu: Three Powers in One Drawer
MONTESQUIEU_BALANCE.pages.INVITATION.des: A magistrate drops the legislative, executive and judicial papers into one drawer and says it will speed things up. You may separate the three powers, balance them through rival factions, or keep Plato's unified arrangement.
MONTESQUIEU_BALANCE.pages.INVITATION.opt: Give each power its own drawer and its own check.
Let opposing factions hold different drawers so no one can close all three.
Refuse the split and keep Plato's single arrangement, giving up this act's fixed link.
MONTESQUIEU_BALANCE.pages.RESULT_SEPARAT: You separate legislation, execution and judgment. Each power can block the others, so speed is traded for a check.
MONTESQUIEU_BALANCE.pages.RESULT_BALANCE: You let rival factions hold different powers. The balance works only while no faction holds two drawers at once.
MONTESQUIEU_BALANCE.pages.RESULT_PRIVILE: You keep the unified arrangement. The route stops here and no fixed link is taken this act.
MONTESQUIEU_BALANCE.pages.RESULT_SEPARAT: Ask Voltaire to review the case
Let the visitor test whether tolerance has a limit here.
MONTESQUIEU_BALANCE.pages.RESULT_BALANCE: Ask Voltaire to review the case
Let the visitor test whether tolerance has a limit here.
MONTESQUIEU_BALANCE.pages.RESULT_PRIVILE: Ask Voltaire to review the case
Let the visitor test whether tolerance has a limit here.
VOLTAIRE_TOLERANCE.title: Voltaire: The Cost of Tolerance
VOLTAIRE_TOLERANCE.pages.INVITATION.desc: A merchant's pamphlet mocks the guild's procession. The guild demands it be burned; the merchant asks only that the argument be answered. Voltaire asks what you will protect.
VOLTAIRE_TOLERANCE.pages.INVITATION.opti: Let the argument stand, even where it wounds the powerful.
Suppress the pamphlet before the procession turns into a riot.
Refuse a verdict and leave the case to Montesquieu's arrangement.
You protect the pamphlet. Tolerance costs the guild its dignity, but the argument can now be answered in the open.
VOLTAIRE_TOLERANCE.pages.RESULT_RESTRICT: You restrict the pamphlet. The procession passes safely, and the argument goes underground where no one can answer it.
You keep the balance and refuse a verdict. The case remains open, and no one owes you an answer.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_LIMITED: Ask Diderot to place the sample
Let the encyclopedist say how this sample enters the system.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_CONTROL: Ask Diderot to place the sample
Let the encyclopedist say how this sample enters the system.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_KEPT.op: Ask Diderot to place the sample
Let the encyclopedist say how this sample enters the system.
BACON_SAMPLE_LEDGER.pages.RESULT_DECLINE: Ask Diderot to place the sample
Let the encyclopedist say how this sample enters the system.
DIDEROT_PRACTICE.title: Diderot: The Sample and the System
DIDEROT_PRACTICE.pages.INVITATION.descri: Diderot looks at the ledger. A single warm-rich sample now has to enter the Encyclopedia -- or stay outside it. He asks what the entry should do.
DIDEROT_PRACTICE.pages.INVITATION.option: Publish the sample under a heading, with its exceptions noted in the same article.
Leave the observation in the ledger; the system waits for more cases.
Decline to turn this case into an entry at all.
DIDEROT_PRACTICE.pages.RESULT_SYSTEM.des: You collect the sample into the system. The entry gains a heading, and the exception travels with it so later readers can see the seam.
DIDEROT_PRACTICE.pages.RESULT_SAMPLE.des: You keep the sample in the ledger. Nothing is published yet, and the system stays open for a second case.
DIDEROT_PRACTICE.pages.RESULT_REFUSE.des: You refuse to summarize. The sample remains unclassified, and no entry claims to have absorbed it.
SMITH_SYMPATHY.title: Adam Smith: Sympathy and Public Action
SMITH_SYMPATHY.pages.INVITATION.descript: A stranger goes bankrupt in the market square. Some onlookers feel for him; others only recalculate the price. Smith asks what order should rest on.
Let fellow-feeling set the standard, even where it favors those near us.
Let prices coordinate strangers and leave sympathy to private life.
Refuse the market question and give up this act's fixed link.
SMITH_SYMPATHY.pages.RESULT_SYMPATHY.des: You ground order in sympathy. Strangers can count on being seen, but fellow-feeling still bends toward those closest to us.
SMITH_SYMPATHY.pages.RESULT_EXCHANGE.des: You rely on exchange and self-interest. Prices coordinate strangers efficiently, and the bankrupt man becomes a line in the ledger.
You keep Plato's arrangement. The market question goes unanswered and no fixed link is taken this act.
SCHELLING_NATURE.title: Schelling: Nature Organizing Itself
SCHELLING_NATURE.pages.INVITATION.descri: A naturalist lays out a fossil sequence: each layer seems to answer the one below it. Schelling asks whether nature is visible spirit, a mechanism, or something Spinoza already settled.
SCHELLING_NATURE.pages.INVITATION.option: Read the sequence as spirit becoming visible in matter.
Keep the sequence mechanical: causes below, effects above.
Refuse the question and stay with Spinoza's one substance.
SCHELLING_NATURE.pages.RESULT_SPIRIT.des: You read nature as visible spirit. The sequence becomes intelligible as self-organization, though the reading risks seeing purpose everywhere.
You keep nature mechanical. The sequence stays predictable, and the appearance of purpose is only an effect of blind causes.
SCHELLING_NATURE.pages.RESULT_KEPT.descr: You keep Spinoza. The fossil question goes unanswered and no fixed link is taken this act.
KIERKEGAARD_FAITH.title: Kierkegaard: The Leap
KIERKEGAARD_FAITH.pages.INVITATION.descr: A parishioner has been told that his duty must be justified to everyone. He cannot do it, and he asks whether that failure is guilt or a sign that the universal is not the whole story.
KIERKEGAARD_FAITH.pages.INVITATION.optio: Suspend the universal for this single existing person.
Demand that the duty be speakable to anyone, whatever it costs him.
Refuse the question and keep the Socratic examination.
KIERKEGAARD_FAITH.pages.RESULT_FAITH.des: You take the leap. The single person stands before what cannot be justified to everyone, and the cost is that no one can take the step for him.
KIERKEGAARD_FAITH.pages.RESULT_ETHICAL.d: You keep the universal. The duty becomes speakable to anyone, and the parishioner must carry what cannot be said in his own case.
KIERKEGAARD_FAITH.pages.RESULT_KEPT.desc: You stay with Socrates. The question remains open, and no fixed link is taken this act.
MARX_ALIENATION.title: Marx: Alienated Labor
MARX_ALIENATION.pages.INVITATION.descrip: A factory inspector shows you the new machines: output has doubled, and the workers say the product no longer belongs to them. Marx asks what this room should record.
MARX_ALIENATION.pages.INVITATION.options: Name the separation between the worker and what the work produces.
Read the machines as a stage that will be surpassed, whatever it costs now.
Refuse the question and stay with Hegel's history of spirit.
You record alienated labor. The worker stands beside a product that is not his, and the machine that should extend him now commands him.
MARX_ALIENATION.pages.RESULT_PROGRESS.de: You record historical progress. The machines become a stage with a direction, and the workers' present loss is booked as a cost of that direction.
MARX_ALIENATION.pages.RESULT_KEPT.descri: You keep Hegel. The question goes unanswered, no fixed link is taken this act, and the journey keeps its ending.
NIETZSCHE_REVALUATION.title: Nietzsche: The Genealogy
NIETZSCHE_REVALUATION.pages.INVITATION.d: A scholar shows you the ledger of a moral society: the same act is praised when the strong do it and called vice when the weak do. Nietzsche asks what this ledger is worth.
NIETZSCHE_REVALUATION.pages.INVITATION.o: Refuse the ledger itself and ask what the valuation serves.
Show how the distinction was made, without pretending it was always there.
Stay with Rousseau and refuse the question.
NIETZSCHE_REVALUATION.pages.RESULT_REVAL: You revalue. The ledger loses its claim to be nature, and every value must now say what it serves.
NIETZSCHE_REVALUATION.pages.RESULT_GENEA: You expose the genealogy. The distinction becomes a dated human act, and the scholar can no longer call it eternal.
You keep Rousseau. The question stays closed, and no fixed link is taken this act.
BENTHAM_UTILITY.title: Bentham: The Calculus
BENTHAM_UTILITY.pages.INVITATION.descrip: A magistrate brings a ledger of pains and pleasures: one severe injury can be offset by many small conveniences. Bentham asks how the room should count it.
BENTHAM_UTILITY.pages.INVITATION.options: Add the ledger up and let the greatest total decide.
Refuse to let one person's injury be cancelled by the total.
Refuse the calculus and keep the Socratic examination.
BENTHAM_UTILITY.pages.RESULT_UTILITY.des: You aggregate. The ledger balances, and the injured party becomes a line that the total can outweigh.
BENTHAM_UTILITY.pages.RESULT_BOUNDARY.de: You keep a boundary. The sum can no longer cancel the one injury, and the calculus must stop at it.
BENTHAM_UTILITY.pages.RESULT_KEPT.descri: You stay with Socrates. The question remains open, and no fixed link is taken this act.
COMTE_POSITIVISM.title: Comte: The Stage Model
COMTE_POSITIVISM.pages.INVITATION.descri: A census clerk has sorted every society into three stages, and one town refuses to fit. Comte asks what the room should record.
COMTE_POSITIVISM.pages.INVITATION.option: File the town as an exception to be corrected later.
Let the town break the model and record what the model cannot hold.
Refuse the question and stay with Bacon's workshop.
COMTE_POSITIVISM.pages.RESULT_STAGES.des: You keep the stages. The town becomes a footnote, and the model keeps its direction at the cost of the case in front of you.
COMTE_POSITIVISM.pages.RESULT_ANOMALY.de: You keep the anomaly. The model must now say what it cannot explain, and the clerk cannot file the town away.
COMTE_POSITIVISM.pages.RESULT_KEPT.descr: You keep Bacon. The question goes unanswered, no question link is taken this act, and the workshop keeps its record.
PEIRCE_INQUIRY.title: Peirce: Fallible Inquiry
PEIRCE_INQUIRY.pages.INVITATION.descript: A surveyor reports a measurement that contradicts the settled table. Peirce asks how the room should hold a belief that may be wrong.
Keep the belief only while its practical consequences hold up.
Let other inquirers try to break it, and keep the result even if it unsettles the table.
Refuse the question and stay with Hume's uncertainty.
PEIRCE_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_TEST.descrip: You test by consequences. The belief becomes a claim about what it lets you do, and the table must answer to that.
PEIRCE_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_COMMUNITY.de: You submit it to the community. The measurement becomes shared work, and no single inquirer can close the question alone.
PEIRCE_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_KEPT.descrip: You keep Hume. The question remains open, and no fixed link is taken this act.
PEIRCE_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_TEST.options: Bring the measurement to James and see what it changes in practice.
PEIRCE_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_COMMUNITY.op: Bring the measurement to James and see what it changes in practice.
PEIRCE_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_KEPT.options: Bring the measurement to James and see what it changes in practice.
JAMES_PRAGMATISM.pages.INVITATION.descri: James listens and asks what difference the belief would make in practice. He offers two ways to answer.
JAMES_PRAGMATISM.pages.INVITATION.option: Put the belief into a shared test and let the result count against it.
Keep the belief as a private working hypothesis.
JAMES_PRAGMATISM.pages.RESULT_PUBLIC.des: You test it publicly. The belief now has a result anyone can check, and a failure would belong to the shared record.
JAMES_PRAGMATISM.pages.RESULT_PRIVATE.de: You keep it private. The belief stays a working hypothesis, and the room cannot claim it has been tested.
DEWEY_PUBLIC_EXPERIMENT.title: Dewey: The Public Experiment
DEWEY_PUBLIC_EXPERIMENT.pages.INVITATION: A school board has tested a new method and published the numbers, but the parents who bear the cost were never asked. Dewey asks what the room should record.
Put the method, its costs, and its failures into a test the affected can join.
Leave the result with the researchers and keep the parents outside.
Refuse the question and stay with Peirce's community of inquirers.
DEWEY_PUBLIC_EXPERIMENT.pages.RESULT_EXP: You make it public. The method becomes a shared experiment, and the parents can contest the cost rather than receive its results.
DEWEY_PUBLIC_EXPERIMENT.pages.RESULT_COM: You keep the community closed. The numbers stay with the researchers, and the parents remain the object of the test.
DEWEY_PUBLIC_EXPERIMENT.pages.RESULT_KEP: You keep Peirce. The question goes unanswered, no question link is taken this act, and the record keeps its inquiry.
HUSSERL_EPOCHE.title: Husserl: The Epochē
HUSSERL_EPOCHE.pages.INVITATION.descript: A student reports what she sees, then catches herself adding what she expected to see. Husserl asks how the room should record the difference.
Keep only what shows itself, and mark the expectation as an addition.
Set aside the question of whether it exists and describe the act of seeing.
Refuse the question and stay with the method of doubt.
HUSSERL_EPOCHE.pages.RESULT_APPEARANCE.d: You describe the appearance. The expectation is marked as an addition, and the thing shows itself only as far as it is given.
HUSSERL_EPOCHE.pages.RESULT_SUSPENSION.d: You suspend the thesis. Existence drops out of the description, and what remains is the act of seeing and what it intends.
HUSSERL_EPOCHE.pages.RESULT_KEPT.descrip: You keep Descartes. The question remains open, and no fixed link is taken this act.
HEIDEGGER_DASEIN.title: Heidegger: Being in the Situation
HEIDEGGER_DASEIN.pages.INVITATION.descri: The seminar has described the appearance cleanly, yet the description leaves out the room it was written in. Heidegger asks what the record should carry.
HEIDEGGER_DASEIN.pages.INVITATION.option: Treat the description as an act inside a situation, with its tools, moods, and projects.
Keep the analysis formal: being-toward, care, and thrownness, without the room.
Refuse the question and stay with the epochē.
You read being from its situation. The description is now an act inside a world, and the room it was written in belongs to the record.
HEIDEGGER_DASEIN.pages.RESULT_DASEIN.des: You describe Dasein's structures. The analysis stays formal, and the concrete room is noted only as an example.
HEIDEGGER_DASEIN.pages.RESULT_KEPT.descr: You keep Husserl. The question remains suspended, and no fixed link is taken this act.
SARTRE_EXISTENCE.title: Sartre: Existence Precedes Essence
SARTRE_EXISTENCE.pages.INVITATION.descri: A student insists she has always been a cautious person, as if the caution came first. Sartre asks what the record should say about that.
SARTRE_EXISTENCE.pages.INVITATION.option: Record the choice first; the character is what the choice has made of it.
Record the choice together with the situation that narrowed it.
Refuse the question and stay with the leap of faith.
You record the choice first. The caution is what she has done with her situation, not a nature that preceded it.
SARTRE_EXISTENCE.pages.RESULT_FREEDOM.de: You record freedom in its situation. The choice is real, and so is the narrowing the record must carry with it.
SARTRE_EXISTENCE.pages.RESULT_KEPT.descr: You keep Kierkegaard. The question goes unanswered, and no fixed link is taken this act.
FREGE_SENSE.title: Frege: Sense and Reference
FREGE_SENSE.pages.INVITATION.description: Two names pick out the same star, yet a reader who learns one learns something the other does not. Frege asks what the record should carry.
FREGE_SENSE.pages.INVITATION.options.SEN: Record what the name means as well as what it picks out.
FREGE_SENSE.pages.INVITATION.options.CON: Record the inference in a notation where every step is checkable.
FREGE_SENSE.pages.INVITATION.options.KEE: Refuse the question and stay with the categories of speech.
FREGE_SENSE.pages.RESULT_SENSE.descripti: You separate sense from reference. The record now carries both what the name means and what it picks out, and the difference is no longer lost.
FREGE_SENSE.pages.RESULT_SCRIPT.descript: You write a concept-script. The inference becomes a chain of checkable steps, and the ordinary name is kept only as an entry point.
FREGE_SENSE.pages.RESULT_KEPT.descriptio: You keep Aristotle. The question remains open, and no fixed link is taken this act.
MERLEAU_PONTY_BODY.title: Merleau-Ponty: The Body as Subject
MERLEAU_PONTY_BODY.pages.INVITATION.desc: The room has measured the hand that reaches for the cup, and the numbers describe a mechanism. Merleau-Ponty asks what the record leaves out.
MERLEAU_PONTY_BODY.pages.INVITATION.opti: The body as subject of perception
Record the hand as the one that perceives, not only as the object measured.
Keep the measurement and treat the reaching as a mechanism it explains.
Refuse the question and stay with the epochē.
MERLEAU_PONTY_BODY.pages.RESULT_BODY.des: You record the body as subject. The hand is the one that reaches and perceives, and the measurement is one of its situations rather than its whole truth.
MERLEAU_PONTY_BODY.pages.RESULT_OBJECTIV: You keep the objective body. The reaching stays a mechanism, and the record notes that the perceiving hand was not entered.
MERLEAU_PONTY_BODY.pages.RESULT_KEPT.des: You keep Husserl. The question remains suspended, and no fixed link is taken this act.
RUSSELL_ANALYSIS.title: Russell: Definite Descriptions
RUSSELL_ANALYSIS.pages.INVITATION.descri: The sentence "the present king of France is bald" seems to say something false, yet there is no king to be bald. Russell asks what the record should analyse.
RUSSELL_ANALYSIS.pages.INVITATION.option: Rewrite the sentence so that existence and uniqueness become explicit claims.
Resolve the sentence into atomic facts and truth-functions.
Refuse the question and stay with sense and reference.
RUSSELL_ANALYSIS.pages.RESULT_DESCRIPTIO: You analyse the description. The sentence no longer presupposes a king; it asserts existence and uniqueness as separate claims, one of which fails.
RUSSELL_ANALYSIS.pages.RESULT_ATOMISM.de: You build a logical atomism. The sentence resolves into atomic facts and truth-functions, and the failure is located in one of them.
RUSSELL_ANALYSIS.pages.RESULT_KEPT.descr: You keep Frege. The question remains open, and no fixed link is taken this act.
WITTGENSTEIN_GAME.title: Wittgenstein: Language Games
WITTGENSTEIN_GAME.pages.INVITATION.descr: The analysis has purified the sentence, yet the room still uses it to ask for a cup. Wittgenstein asks what the record should keep.
WITTGENSTEIN_GAME.pages.INVITATION.optio: Record the sentence inside the practice that gives it a use.
Record the sentence as a picture that must share a form with the fact.
Refuse the question and stay with the logical analysis.
WITTGENSTEIN_GAME.pages.RESULT_GAME.desc: You record the language game. The sentence is now part of an activity, and the request for a cup is what gives it sense.
WITTGENSTEIN_GAME.pages.RESULT_PICTURE.d: You record the picture theory. The sentence is a picture of the fact, and the room notes that the practice of asking was not entered.
WITTGENSTEIN_GAME.pages.RESULT_KEPT.desc: You keep Russell. The question goes unanswered, and no question link is taken this act.
SAUSSURE_SIGN.title: Saussure: Language and Speech
SAUSSURE_SIGN.pages.INVITATION.descripti: The room has a written rule and a living speaker who breaks it. Saussure asks what the record should separate.
SAUSSURE_SIGN.pages.INVITATION.options.L: Record the shared system apart from this speaker's use of it.
SAUSSURE_SIGN.pages.INVITATION.options.S: Record that the link between sound and meaning is conventional.
SAUSSURE_SIGN.pages.INVITATION.options.K: Refuse the question and stay with the categories of speech.
SAUSSURE_SIGN.pages.RESULT_LANGUE.descri: You separate language from speech. The shared system is recorded apart from the speaker's use, and the breaking becomes a fact about speech.
SAUSSURE_SIGN.pages.RESULT_SIGN.descript: You mark the sign as arbitrary. The link between sound and meaning is recorded as convention, and the rule can change without the world changing.
SAUSSURE_SIGN.pages.RESULT_KEPT.descript: You keep Aristotle. The question goes unanswered, and no question link is taken this act.
LEVI_STRAUSS_MYTH.title: Levi-Strauss: The Structure of Myth
LEVI_STRAUSS_MYTH.pages.INVITATION.descr: Two versions of the same story differ in every detail, yet repeat the same opposition. Levi-Strauss asks what the record should keep.
LEVI_STRAUSS_MYTH.pages.INVITATION.optio: Record the recurring oppositions and how the versions transform them.
Record the versions as events in a sequence with causes.
Refuse the question and stay with language and speech.
LEVI_STRAUSS_MYTH.pages.RESULT_STRUCTURE: You read the myth structurally. The versions are transformations of one set of oppositions, and the differences are kept as variations rather than noise.
LEVI_STRAUSS_MYTH.pages.RESULT_HISTORY.d: You keep a historical reading. The versions are dated and causally ordered, and the recurring opposition is noted but not made the object.
LEVI_STRAUSS_MYTH.pages.RESULT_KEPT.desc: You keep Saussure. The question goes unanswered, and no fixed link is taken this act.
FOUCAULT_POWER.title: Foucault: Power and Knowledge
FOUCAULT_POWER.pages.INVITATION.descript: The prison record lists every inmate, and the list itself changes how they are treated. Foucault asks what the record should say about that.
Record the list as an instrument that produces what it describes.
Record the timetable, the inspection, and the examination as the machinery.
Refuse the question and stay with the revaluation of values.
FOUCAULT_POWER.pages.RESULT_POWER.descri: You link power to knowledge. The list is recorded as an instrument that produces the inmate it describes, not as a neutral description.
FOUCAULT_POWER.pages.RESULT_DISCIPLINE.d: You describe the disciplinary institution. The timetable and the examination are recorded as the machinery, and the record notes that the list was not analysed.
FOUCAULT_POWER.pages.RESULT_KEPT.descrip: You keep Nietzsche. The question goes unanswered, and no fixed link is taken this act.
DERRIDA_DECONSTRUCTION.title: Derrida: Deconstruction
The myth is read as a structure, and the structure keeps a centre it cannot name. Derrida asks what the record should do with that centre.
Record the pair and show which term the text keeps subordinate.
Record meaning as deferred, never fully present in either term.
Refuse the question and stay with the structural reading.
DERRIDA_DECONSTRUCTION.pages.RESULT_BINA: You undo the binary hierarchy. The pair is recorded with the term the text subordinates, and the hierarchy is left visible rather than resolved.
DERRIDA_DECONSTRUCTION.pages.RESULT_DIFF: You mark differance. Meaning is recorded as deferred, and the record notes that the structural reading was not abandoned.
DERRIDA_DECONSTRUCTION.pages.RESULT_KEPT: You keep Levi-Strauss. The question goes unanswered, and no question link is taken this act.
DELEUZE_DIFFERENCE.title: Deleuze: Difference and Repetition
DELEUZE_DIFFERENCE.pages.INVITATION.desc: The same event returns, and each return differs. Deleuze asks what the record should count as real.
DELEUZE_DIFFERENCE.pages.INVITATION.opti: Record the divergence as primary and identity as a result.
Record the connections as a network with no centre or hierarchy.
Refuse the question and stay with nature as visible spirit.
DELEUZE_DIFFERENCE.pages.RESULT_DIFFEREN: You record difference before identity. The divergence is primary, and identity is noted as what the repetition produces.
You record a rhizome. The connections are recorded without centre, and the record notes that identity was not derived.
DELEUZE_DIFFERENCE.pages.RESULT_KEPT.des: You keep Schelling. The question goes unanswered, and no question link is taken this act.
GADAMER_FUSION.title: Gadamer: Fusion of Horizons
GADAMER_FUSION.pages.INVITATION.descript: The text was written for another age, and you read it from yours. Gadamer asks what the record should make of that distance.
Record your question and the text's answer as one conversation.
Record how the tradition has already shaped what you can hear in the text.
Refuse the question and stay with being-in-the-world.
GADAMER_FUSION.pages.RESULT_FUSION.descr: You fuse the horizons. Your question and the text's answer are recorded as one conversation, and the distance is kept as what makes it possible.
GADAMER_FUSION.pages.RESULT_HISTORY.desc: You mark effective history. The record shows how the tradition shaped your reading before you began, and notes that the fusion itself was not entered.
GADAMER_FUSION.pages.RESULT_KEPT.descrip: You keep Heidegger. The question goes unanswered, and no question link is taken this act.
